declared_purpose: Provide semantic memory across conversations using local embeddings, with store/search/forget tools, optional automatic capture, relevant-memory recall, default in-memory storage and optional persistent Qdrant storage. These capabilities are explicit; regex selection, whole-message capture, thresholds, payload breadth and logging are implementation choices (SKILL.md:16-26, 50-87).

data_operations.data_scope: Qdrant URL, collection name, memory capacity and capture/recall settings.
data_operations.condition: Plugin registration. Defaults are declared in the schema; hooks execute only when their configuration values are truthy.

data_operations.source: Documented npm installation commands and dependency declarations.
data_operations.data_scope: Dependency identifiers and downloaded packages; exact installation request contents are not supplied.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Documented npmjs.com service and local installation.
data_operations.condition: Someone follows the installation instructions; this is separate from ordinary memory operations.

data_operations.operation: Initialize and cache the embedding model
data_operations.data_scope: Documented approximately 25 MB model download and local model cache. No conversation upload to Hugging Face is explicitly implemented.
data_operations.condition: First embedding initialization; initialization retries up to three times. Download and cache internals belong to an unsupplied dependency.

data_operations.source: Memory text, search/forget queries, command arguments and lifecycle-hook prompt/text inputs.
data_operations.data_scope: Input text transformed through mean pooling and normalization into embedding vectors; configured vector dimension is 384.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local Transformers.js pipeline; vectors subsequently reach the selected database through store/search operations.
data_operations.condition: Any path calling embeddings.embed(). The source invokes a local pipeline rather than a hosted embedding API.

data_operations.source: memory_store parameters or remember command arguments.
data_operations.data_scope: memory_store strips HTML tags/control characters, normalizes whitespace, accepts 1-10000 cleaned characters and checks duplicates at 0.95. remember trims arguments, has no source-level length cap or duplicate check, and assigns importance 0.8.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local processing followed by the selected memory backend.
data_operations.condition: Explicit tool or command invocation. Sanitization does not remove PII.

data_operations.operation: Read and select conversation text automatically
data_operations.data_scope: User-role string content and text blocks. Whole matching strings are selected using length, markup, emoji and keyword/PII-pattern checks; default maximum is 500 characters. Chinese-character presence changes the minimum length. Selected text is not sanitized.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local capture buffer, embedding pipeline and selected memory backend.
data_operations.condition: autoCapture truthy, successful agent event with messages, capture filter passes, and no duplicate at 0.95. Capture is declared disabled by default.

data_operations.source: remember command text and automatically captured user text.
data_operations.data_scope: Heuristic preference, decision, entity, fact or other labels derived from regex matches. Importance values on these paths are fixed assignments, not inferred importance.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Memory record metadata; categories can later appear in caller responses, agent context and logs.
data_operations.condition: Command storage or successful automatic capture. memory_store instead accepts a caller-supplied category, defaulting to other.

data_operations.source: Entries submitted by the tool, command or capture hook.
data_operations.data_scope: UUID, text, embedding vector, category, importance and creation timestamp.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: MemoryDB.memoryStore array; documented as cleared on process restart.
data_operations.condition: qdrantUrl is absent/falsy or equals :memory:. Default capacity is 1000; capacity eviction is disabled for maxSize >= 999999.

data_operations.operation: Contact Qdrant for administration and statistics
data_operations.source: Configured database endpoint and collection name.
data_operations.data_scope: Startup getCollections health request, collection existence/schema operations, and collection metadata used to obtain points_count.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Server selected by qdrantUrl and local plugin process. The startup collection-list result is not otherwise used.
data_operations.condition: Qdrant mode. Collection initialization occurs lazily before database operations; stats invokes count().

data_operations.operation: Send memory records to Qdrant storage
data_operations.source: Entries submitted by any storage path.
data_operations.data_scope: UUID and vector plus payload containing full text, category, importance and creation timestamp.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Configured qdrantUrl server, in cfg.collectionName or openclaw_memories. Server may be local or remote; persistent storage is an explicit option.
data_operations.condition: Qdrant mode and successful store operation. The package configures no external record expiry or capacity eviction.

data_operations.operation: Search memories and derive relevance scores
data_operations.data_scope: Local mode computes cosine similarity over stored vectors. Qdrant mode sends vector, result limit and threshold with with_payload:true, then reads IDs, text, category, importance, timestamps and scores. No owner/session filter is supplied.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local search caller; in Qdrant mode, the configured server receives the vector and returns payloads to the plugin process. Raw query text is not an explicit search-request field.
data_operations.condition: Explicit search, duplicate detection, query-based forgetting, recall hook or CLI search.

data_operations.operation: Return requested results to callers and CLI
data_operations.source: Stored or matched memories and database count.
data_operations.data_scope: Search returns memory text/categories/scores and tool or CLI IDs. Duplicate rejection and query-based deletion may return full existing text; forget candidates include full text. Store acknowledgements quote up to 50 characters. CLI stats prints the count.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Invoking tool/command caller or CLI stdout. Further sharing or persistence is not established.
data_operations.condition: Corresponding explicit invocation and result branch.

data_operations.operation: Inject recalled memories into agent context
data_operations.source: Entire event.prompt and matching memory records.
data_operations.data_scope: Prompt embedding; up to three matches at threshold 0.3; category and up to 500 characters per recalled memory, wrapped as historical context.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: OpenClaw before_agent_start caller through prependContext. Any downstream model-provider disclosure is unknown.
data_operations.condition: autoRecall truthy, prompt length at least five, and nonempty search results. The schema declares autoRecall true by default.

data_operations.source: memoryId, query-selected match, or local capacity policy.
data_operations.data_scope: Local deletion removes an array entry; capacity eviction removes the oldest-created record. Qdrant deletion sends the selected ID.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local memory array or configured Qdrant collection.
data_operations.condition: Explicit memoryId; or query search yielding exactly one result above 0.95; or bounded local storage reaching capacity. Other query matches return candidates instead.

data_operations.source: Configuration, capture text/category, recall counts and caught errors.
data_operations.data_scope: Full configured Qdrant URL at startup; first 50 characters and category of newly captured memories at debug level; counts, status and error messages.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: api.logger. Its actual sink, retention and access controls are unspecified.
data_operations.condition: Applicable startup, successful capture/recall or error branch; actual debug emission depends on host logging.

data_operations.operation: Process fixed test fixtures and print test results
data_operations.data_scope: Synthetic sanitation/category/capture inputs, assertion messages, expected/actual values and aggregate counts.
data_operations.condition: Standalone execution of the test file. Its explicit calls use exported helpers; plugin registration is not invoked.

potential_excess.data_scope: First 50 characters and inferred category of automatically captured user text, potentially including PII.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: api.logger debug channel, separate from the selected memory backend; log persistence is unknown.
potential_excess.condition: autoCapture enabled, a new memory successfully stored, and debug output accepted by the host.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Automatic memory capture requires storing selected information; content-bearing diagnostic logs are an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Capture, categorize, deduplicate and store the memory.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Log a content-free capture count or status instead of the text excerpt and category.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep the stored memory and capture behavior intact.

potential_excess.data_scope: Full cfg.qdrantUrl, including URL userinfo or credential-bearing parameters if present.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: api.logger info channel during Qdrant-mode registration.
potential_excess.condition: Qdrant mode; credential exposure additionally depends on credentials being embedded in the configured URL.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Selecting and diagnosing the storage endpoint does not require logging embedded credentials.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Connect using the configured endpoint and report storage mode or connection status.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Log mode/status only, or an allowlisted endpoint representation with credential-bearing components removed.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Continue supplying the original URL internally to QdrantClient.

potential_excess.data_scope: Existing memory text, category, importance and timestamps fetched solely to establish duplicate existence.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Configured Qdrant server response into the plugin process.
potential_excess.condition: Automatic capture performs its one-result duplicate search; this caller uses only existing.length.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Duplicate detection is necessary to the implemented capture behavior; full payload retrieval is extra data within that required search.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Search the candidate vector at threshold 0.95 and skip storage when a match exists.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Add an existence-only search path that omits payload retrieval and payload mapping.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve the threshold, result limit and skip behavior. Keep payload-dependent feedback on other callers separately supported.

potential_excess.data_scope: importance and createdAt fields retrieved with search results.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Configured Qdrant server response into the plugin process.
potential_excess.condition: Payload-bearing searches; current result consumers do not use these fields.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Search, recall and candidate identification use IDs, text, categories and scores. Fetching unused metadata is a payload-breadth choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Retrieve fields required by each search consumer.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use per-consumer payload projection and omit importance/createdAt from search responses.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain timestamps in storage where needed for local eviction, and preserve fields actually used in caller responses or recall context.

potential_excess.data_scope: Incidental clauses or identifiers in an otherwise capture-worthy user message.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local memoryStore, or full-text/vector disclosure and retention at the configured Qdrant collection.
potential_excess.condition: autoCapture enabled and a whole string passes a trigger although only part contains the intended important information.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The UI describes saving important information. Whole-string capture can retain unrelated material. Email/phone storage itself is explicitly disclosed and may be necessary.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Remember the intended fact, preference, decision or entity.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Select the memory-bearing portion before embedding and storage when unrelated material can be identified reliably.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve intended identifiers, context and explicitly requested verbatim memories; narrow only material unrelated to the required memory.

unknowns: Dependency and native-install implementation source is absent. Exact download requests, additional network behavior, cache operations and telemetry cannot be determined from dependency metadata (package-lock.json:73-118).

OpenClaw source is absent. Schema-default application, event.prompt composition, event.messages history scope, caller authorization and downstream handling of tool returns/prependContext remain unknown (openclaw.plugin.json:19-31; index.js:529-575).

All operations use the instance database and configured collection without an owner filter. Whether independent users share them, and whether the host supplies isolation, is unresolved; cross-user disclosure cannot be established from this package alone (index.js:101-110, 153-158, 320-324).

The actual qdrantUrl endpoint, transport/authentication configuration, server access controls, retention, backups and deletion guarantees are unavailable. A delete request does not establish erasure of every copy (index.js:34-45, 187-191).

Logger destination, retention, access controls and debug-level handling are unknown. Error-message contents are dependency-dependent and may contain additional data (index.js:330-340, 546-547, 584-587).

MemoryDB.search references api in its catch block outside register(api)'s parameter scope; no module-level binding is supplied. Its intended logging and empty-result fallback are therefore unreliable on the error path (index.js:171-174, 320-320).
memory_forget ignores the local delete() boolean and does not verify remote erasure. Its success response alone cannot confirm that a record existed or was fully removed (index.js:177-191, 438-440).
